text:
anya: Heads up — CI went red on my tiny annotations PR #4287 after merging. Local runs fine. Mypy failure only in CI:
ci-bot: build/6482 — precommit -> mypy: FAILED

ERROR: tests/integration/test_kvcache.py:12: error: Incompatible types in assignment (expression has type "None", variable has type "Mapping[str, Any]")
Found 1 error in 1 file (checked 124 source files)

anya: I didn't touch that file. Tests all passed locally. Any quick triage ideas? :thinking_face:
sam: can you paste the full CI failure URL? sometimes environment/mypy cache causes weirdness. :eyes:
anya: https://ci.redwood.internal/build/6482 — attaching the failure snippet above. I suspect a different mypy version in CI? We pinned mypy in pyproject but maybe pre-commit runs a different one.
mike: if local passes, first try a rerun with clean cache. CI has an option to rerun job without cache — can you trigger that? If it flips green, it's probably cache/version mismatch.
linh: also check pre-commit and tox envs. We had a similar flake last week where pre-commit used system mypy 0.991 but pyproject pinned 1.2.0. Run: `python -m pipx run --spec "mypy==1.2.0" mypy src/` to reproduce locally.
anya: kicked off a manual rerun (no-cache). pinging here so folks see. :thumbsup:
ci-bot: build/6482 (rerun) — still FAILED — same error trace.
sam: okay not cache. Next best is bisecting commits on the branch. Any recent churn around kvcache typing? anya: No, same branch only annotation tweak in pr header.
mike: try running the exact pre-commit pipeline locally: `pre-commit run --all-files --hook-stage manual` and specifically `pre-commit run mypy --all-files` — sometimes CI runs with slightly different interpreter path causing Optional vs None inference.
linh: also dump mypy --show-traceback and `mypy --version` in CI job — can add a debug step to the workflow and re-run. I'll add a quick commit to the branch to print versions.
anya: added debug step and re-ran. CI output: `mypy 1.2.0` in CI. Weird.
mike: hmm. Could it be test import order? Sometimes tests that set typing.TYPE_CHECKING flags or monkeypatching alters inference. Is there any test fixture that mutates kvcache during import? If so, the stubs could be different on CI due to installed extras.
sam: try running `PYTHONPATH=src/ pytest tests/integration/test_kvcache.py::test_insert --capture=no -k kvcache` locally to mirror CI boundaries.
anya: ran that, still green locally.
linh: next step: run mypy check in a clean docker image that matches CI runner (ubuntu + python 3.11). I can spin one and run the same commands; I'll report back in ~20m.
mike: if that reproduces, we can bisect. If not, maybe transient flake in generated stub inference — fallback is to pin stricter types in the test to avoid None assignment, but that's a last resort.
anya: thanks — appreciate the quick triage. If it stays failing after docker test, please shout and we'll bisect with `git bisect` using `./scripts/mypy-check.sh` as the test command.
linh: update: in docker matching CI I can reproduce the error. Investigating differences now. Found that one dependency (redis-py in CI) is older in the runner image, shipping a stub that types connection return as Optional; locally you have newer version that types as Mapping. Adding pinned dependency or a local stub fix likely to resolve.
sam: good catch. Two options: pin redis version in pyproject/ci deps, or narrow our annotation in the test to accept Optional. Which do we prefer?
mike: prefer pinning in the CI env for now so we keep stricter typing in code. open a small PR to pin test deps and rerun.
anya: opened PR #4290 to pin redis to >=5.2,<5.3 in ci-deps — cc @linh. Triggering CI.
ci-bot: build/6491 for PR #4290 — all checks passed :white_check_mark:
anya: merging the pin PR now. Thanks everyone. Saved a full bisect. :rocket:
